market.what: corrosion-inhibiting concrete admixtures + surface-applied inhibitors (calcium nitrite, amino alcohols, MCI), world
market.method: report $479M (VMR says $1.30B, outlier); bottom-up est. ~0.1% of 14 bn m3/yr concrete x 15 L/m3 x ~$1.6/L = ~$0.35B

value.logic: US bridge corrosion $8.3B/yr direct (FHWA); world ~3x = ~$25B; better inhibitor on new and repaired salt-exposed concrete cuts that ~10% at maturity (est.)
value.revenue_logic: ~6% share of ~$0.5B admixture market by yr 7 at price parity with calcium nitrite (~$20-25/m3)
value.margin_logic: admixture sold through Sika/Saint-Gobain-type channels; small aryl phosphonate made in 1-2 steps

trend.drivers: aging bridges ($260B repair backlog US, 41,677 poor bridges); de-icing salt; marine and coastal infrastructure

competition.notes: no funded startup found with a new molecular rebar inhibitor; Sika (owns MBS MasterLife) and Saint-Gobain/GCP dominate; the threat is non-steel rebar

lab.test: LPR/EIS in simulated pore solution (sat. Ca(OH)2 + NaCl) + ASTM G180 slurry test + ASTM C494 set/strength check; G109 macrocell beams run on for C1582 (months-years)
lab.logic: synth 5 wk + electrochem 4 wk + 28-day strength; synth ~$15k + tests ~$15k (est.)

sale.gates: ASTM C1582 needs G109 macrocell data (long run); state DOT approved-product lists; TSCA PMN for new substance; faster via repair/parking market
sources: https://Transportation.Ky.Gov/Construction/Special Notes and Special Provisions/SPECIAL NOTE 2CC FOR CORROSION INHIBITORS.pdf
